explain.say: Here are the Decomposers. Decompose means rot, or break down. Mushrooms, mould, bacteria and earthworms feed on dead leaves, droppings and old food, breaking them into tiny bits. Have you seen fuzzy mould on old bread? That is a decomposer at work!

faq.q: What is the difference between a producer and a consumer?
faq.a: A producer, like a plant, makes its own food from sunlight. A consumer, like an animal, cannot make food, so it eats plants or other animals.
A decomposer is a living thing that breaks down dead plants, dead animals and waste, such as fungi like mushrooms and mould, bacteria, and helpers like earthworms.

faq.q: What would happen if nothing rotted?
faq.a: Dead leaves, bodies and waste would pile up everywhere, and the goodness locked inside them would never get back to the soil, so new plants would starve.
No. A mushroom is a fungus. Fungi cannot make food from sunlight; they feed by breaking down dead things, so they are decomposers.
Yes. Humans cannot make food from sunlight, so we eat plants and, for many people, animals too. That makes us consumers.

facts: Fungi are not plants: they cannot photosynthesise and feed by breaking down other material.
A teaspoon of healthy soil can contain billions of microorganisms, more than the number of people on Earth.

quiz.say: Fuzzy green mould grows on an old orange. What is the mould?
quiz.why: Mould breaks down old food, so it is a decomposer.

wrong.0: Producers make food from sunlight; mould cannot.
wrong.1: Mould is grouped with decomposers because it breaks down dead or old things.

quiz.say: Which of these is a producer?
quiz.why: A maize plant makes its own food from sunlight.

wrong.0: A goat eats plants, so it is a consumer.
wrong.2: A mushroom breaks down dead things, so it is a decomposer.
